en.headline: HKUST student reports losing HK$1.11 million in phone scam
en.dek: A 19-year-old mainland student told police early Sunday that a caller posing as an Immigration officer demanded a deposit and claimed to be watching her by webcam.
body: Police said they received a report at about 1am on Sunday from a 19-year-old woman at student halls on University Road in Sai Kung. Officers classified the case as obtaining property by deception. Tseung Kwan O district crime officers are investigating.

According to police accounts carried by local outlets, the woman, a mainland student at the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology, said she had earlier received a call from someone claiming to be an Immigration Department officer. The caller alleged she was linked to a money-laundering case on the mainland and demanded HK$1.11 million as a so-called deposit.

The caller also claimed to be watching her through a webcam, including while she transferred money, reports said. She told her family she needed funds for a school exchange programme, obtained the sum and sent it as instructed.

She later saw similar scam methods on TikTok, suspected she had been deceived and reported the matter at the halls. Police said they were tracing the callers and the money. Authorities have repeatedly warned that government departments do not demand deposits by phone or ask people to keep such contacts secret.

zh.headline: 科大19歲內地生報稱遭假入境人員騙去111萬
zh.dek: 女生週日凌晨在西貢大學道宿舍報案，指有人自稱入境處人員，訛稱她涉及洗黑錢案並索取保證金，又聲稱以網絡鏡頭監視匯款。
body: 警方表示，週日凌晨約1時在西貢大學道1號科技大學學生宿舍接獲一名19歲女子報案，案件列作以欺騙手段取得財產，交由將軍澳警區刑事調查隊跟進。
本地傳媒引述調查消息指，事主為科技大學內地學生。她較早前接到陌生來電，對方自稱入境處人員，指她與內地一宗洗黑錢案有關，要求交出111萬港元作為所謂保證金，並聲稱透過網絡攝影機監視她的行動，包括匯款過程。
報道指，事主向家人隱瞞來電內容，以參加學校交流活動為由取得款項後，按指示匯出。她其後在短片平台看到類似騙案手法，懷疑受騙，於宿舍報案。
警方正追查涉案人士及款項去向。當局多次提醒，政府部門不會以電話索取保證金，亦不會要求市民對來電保密。
